from the very beginning, the early christian communities realised the importance of sunday. it is the day of jesus’ resurrection, a day of joy and rest, as well as charity, sunday is the lord’s day, the day when we are called to remember what god has done and continues to do for us. this, then, is the day the lord’s people are called to keep holy together. the observance begins with the evening of the preceding day. early christians did what jesus had asked them to do; they gathered and celebrated the meal jesus had shared wit them, the eucharist. we also know this as the mass. this gathering of the community on a sunday to celebrate the eucharist gave rise to a basic principle of the church: there can be no sunday without the eucharist and eucharist without an assembly of the faithful. this principle endures to this day. it led voltaire to declare ‘if you want to kill christianity, you must abolish sunday. ’ as members of the christian community, we are each called to gather with the rest of our faith community on a sunday to celebrate the eucharist. the sunday mass is the place where we gather as a parish, as a community, as the people of god. this is at the heart of the life of the church. it is the highpoint of our christian life, where god nourishes us to go out and live as christians (catholicbishops.ie)

. next tue nov 2nd is the commemoration of all the faithful departed: mass at 11 am & 6 pm. november - remembering those we love! november has a special place in our hearts. as the evenings grow darker and the years draw towards its close, we find ourselves thinking of those who are no longer with us. all of us have people we miss: a husband or wife, a parent, a brother or sister, a friend or neighbour. we remember their voices, their smiles, the little things they did, and the memories that remain with us. sometimes it is only when we hear a familiar song, visit a favourite place or sit quietly at home that we realise just how much we still miss them. during november, we are invited to remember our dead in a special way. we light candles, visit their graves and pray for them, trusting them to the loving care of god. grief may never completely leave us, but neither does love. the people we have loved remain part of who we are. may this month bring comfort to those who mourn gratitude for the lives we have shared, and hope in the promise that love is stronger than death. cahersiveen
